2610.08501.title: Language-model ratings of depression reflect the rater more than the patient
2610.08501.paper_summary: Depression has no diagnostic blood test. Language models promise tireless, consistent assessment, but can accurate raters disagree about individuals? We pre-registered 880 language-model raters, crossing 11 open models with prompting and scoring choices, and applied them to 189 interviews against the eight-item Patient Health Questionnaire. Model choice explained 30.0% of summed-symptom score variance, stable participant differences 10.5%. Two randomly drawn raters with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) >= 0.70 disagreed on screening decisions for 40% of participants, on average. Average over-rating governed how many were flagged, yet equal-capacity raters chose differently for about one participant in five. A locked analysis of 86 new interviews reproduced the main pre-registered findings. Exploratory recalibration with 40 labelled participants raised accuracy from about 60% to 75% and halved disagreement, leaving one participant in five decided differently. Calibration repaired much of the rater dependence without securing agreement about individuals.
2610.08501.paper_summary_zh: 憂鬱症沒有診斷性的血液測試。語言模型承諾提供不知疲倦且一致的評估，但準確的評估者能否對個體達成共識？我們預先註冊了880名語言模型評估者，交叉使用11個開放模型與提示和評分選擇，並將其應用於189次訪談，對照八項患者健康問卷。模型選擇解釋了30.0%的總症狀分數變異，穩定的參與者差異為10.5%。兩名隨機抽取的評估者，其接收者操作特徵曲線下面積（AUC）>= 0.70，對40%的參與者的篩查決策存在分歧，平均而言。平均過度評分決定了有多少被標記，然而能力相等的評估者對約五分之一的參與者做出了不同的選擇。對86個新訪談的鎖定分析重現了主要的預先註冊發現。對40名標記參與者的探索性重新校準將準確度從約60%提高到75%，並將分歧減半，仍然有五分之一的參與者做出了不同的決定。校準修復了大部分的評估者依賴性，但未能確保對個體的共識。
2610.08501.author: Baihan Lin et.al.
